A clinical opinion and a legal finding are not the same document

Most psychiatric reports entering court were never written for court. This pathway exists to close that gap — from both ends.

The method is deliberately unglamorous: defined questions, documented reasoning, traceable sources, and conclusions stated at the confidence the evidence supports. That structure is what makes an opinion admissible — and what protects the clinician who signed it.

Nothing is imported wholesale. Programmes are built around the legal frameworks practitioners actually appear under, then aligned with international forensic standards.

“We’re not just training psychiatrists — we’re building the professional standard where clinical expertise becomes court-admissible evidence”MISSION · MEDLEX SOLUTIONS

Who this pathway is for

PsychiatristsReceiving legal referrals and needing a report structure that holds under cross-examination.
PsychologistsWorking in court-directed assessment and needing a documented methodology.
TraineesBuilding forensic competence early, and in the right order.
Legal professionalsReading psychiatric reports, testing them, and instructing experts well.

Designed for professionals who receive the questions courts ask. Not for the general public.

Four levels. Each one prepares you for the next.

A progressive framework built on recognised professional competency frameworks, so that learning is consistent, cumulative and measurable. Enter at the level that matches your practice.

4Progressive levels, from a single masterclass to advanced certification
Level 1

Foundation Masterclasses

Single topic · 3–6 hours · CPD-focused

Fourteen masterclasses already designed across three core themes — the structured entry point to the pathway. Each takes one question a court asks and teaches the reasoning behind a defensible answer.

Level 2

Professional Skills Programmes

Multi-session · 10–14 hours · materials and assignments between sessions

Practical skills development and the pathway's primary offering. Four to six workshops around a single simulated case, with work produced between sessions and reviewed in the next. Home of Writing Psychiatric Evidence.

Level 3

Foundations of Forensic Psychiatry & Medico-Legal Practice

Three-month blended programme

Structured professional competence across the medico-legal field: assessment, formulation, report writing, and giving evidence — with supervision and assessed work throughout.

Level 4

Advanced Professional Certification

Twelve-month programme · future pathway

The advanced specialist pathway, built in sequence once the earlier levels are established: supervised casework, assessed reports, and a portfolio of practice.

Flagship programme · Level 2

Writing Psychiatric Evidence

Eight modules across two live teaching days, separated by a structured two-week practical assignment. Participants leave having produced a complete psychiatric medico-legal report.

  • One case, start to finish. The whole programme works on a single simulated medico-legal case file, MLC-100, with eight professionally developed documents — no unrelated examples.
  • Applied, not theoretical. Participants move from analysing the case material to writing the report using a structured professional methodology.
  • The full package. Educational framework, report-writing checklist, pre-course reading, session summaries, between-session assignments, self-assessment tools, the complete case file and a model psychiatric report.
  • Bilingual. Delivered in English and Arabic, each written natively.

One knowledge base. Two professional audiences.

The content is developed once and adapted for the people who use it. The knowledge, principles and case material are the same; only the language, emphasis and examples change.

For clinicians

Psychiatrists, psychologists and trainees learn to answer the legal question as a clinician: what the court is actually asking, what the evidence supports, how to write it so it survives challenge, and how to give it in the witness box.

Assessment · Formulation · Report · Evidence

For legal professionals

Judges, prosecutors and counsel learn to read a psychiatric report critically: what a sound opinion looks like, where reports typically fail, how to instruct an expert well, and how to test the evidence in cross-examination.

Instruction · Reading · Testing · Cross-examination

Built by someone who has been cross-examined

Every programme in this pathway is written and taught by a UK-trained Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist whose own opinions have been examined before Mental Health Tribunals, Magistrates' and Crown Courts, and the Parole Board.

Dr Ahmed AbouelghitConsultant Forensic Psychiatrist · Founder and Programme DirectorRead the full profile

Court-tested, not textbook

The failures the programmes teach around are the ones that actually happen in hearings: the undefined question, the missing reasoning, the conclusion that went further than the evidence.

Tribunal · Magistrates' · Crown Court · Parole Board

Built for the jurisdiction

International forensic standards applied to the legal frameworks practitioners here actually appear under — UK, Egyptian and Gulf — so what is taught can be used on Monday.

Local frameworks · International standards

A documented method

Defined questions, documented reasoning, traceable sources, calibrated conclusions. A method the clinician can explain and stand behind when it is challenged.

Admissible · Defensible

Recognition built in sequence

Academic partnerships and supervision protocols are being developed step by step, so that recognition follows the quality of the work rather than preceding it. No claims made before they are true.

Questions.

Who is this pathway for?

Psychiatrists and psychologists who write, or expect to write, for courts and tribunals; psychiatry trainees building forensic competence; and legal professionals who instruct, read and test psychiatric evidence. It is not designed for the general public.

What is available now?

The pathway is taking a waitlist. The first cohort of Writing Psychiatric Evidence and the opening Foundation Masterclasses will be announced to the waitlist before anywhere else.

How are programmes delivered?

Live and interactive, online. Masterclasses run as single sessions of three to six hours; skills programmes run across several sessions with assignments in between; the three-month programme blends live teaching with supervised work.

Is it in English or Arabic?

Both. Each programme is delivered in English and in Arabic as separate, natively written versions — not a translation of one into the other.

Do I need to be in the UK, Egypt or Qatar?

No. Online delivery is open worldwide. Where a face-to-face element is offered, its location and dates are stated on the programme page.

Is the pathway accredited or CPD-certified?

Programmes are independent and not currently accredited by any college or regulator. Certificates of completion are issued. Formal CPD recognition and accreditation are being developed in sequence and will be stated clearly on each programme page once in place.

Does MedLex provide expert reports or legal advice?

This pathway is education. MedLex does not provide legal advice and does not act for individuals in their own legal matters. Institutional training and advisory work is described on the Institutional page.
